column2: AI-Powered Assistive Technologies for Visual Impairment
column3: Prudhvi Naayini, Praveen Kumar Myakala, Chiranjeevi Bura, Anil Kumar Jonnalagadda, Srikanth Kamatala
column4: Review development, applications and impact of AI-powered tools (CV, NLP, wearables) for visual impairment.
column5: Narrative review of AI-based smart glasses, smartphone apps, navigation aids, deep learning, multimodal interfaces
column6: AI enables object recognition, scene description, TTS navigation, improving independence, access to education or work, highlights ethical, affordability, and adaptability issues
column7: Calls for interdisciplinary work, focus on ethics, affordability, equitable access, and robust deployment in diverse environments
column10: AI-Powered Assistive Technologies for Visual Impairment.pdf

column2: Technological Advancements in Human Navigation for the Visually Impaired: A Systematic Review
column3: Casanova E., Guffanti D., Hidalgo L.
column4: Evaluate effectiveness and functionality of navigation systems for visually impaired people (2019–2024)
column5: PRISMA 2020 systematic review; 58 articles from Dimensions, WoS, Scopus; bibliometric and comparative analysis
column6: Shows rapid growth in navigation tech, strong role of haptics and smartphones (79% experimental, 87% haptics, 40% smartphones); but large gaps in digital accessibility and adapted support systems
column7: Emphasizes need for further tech and social solutions to ensure equal opportunities and autonomy for blind users
column10: Technological Advancements in Human Navigation for the Visually Impaired: A Systematic Review.pdf

column2: Review of Navigation Assistive Tools and Technologies for the Visually Impaired
column3: Messaoudi M.D., Ménéla s B., Mcheick H.
column4: Present state-of-the-art mobility and navigation assistive tools (indoor/outdoor) and analyze methods and feedback modalities
column5: Literature review of multiple mobility technologies, locations (indoor/outdoor), feedback modes (audio, haptic, etc.)
column6: Details many devices and methods; highlights persistent mobility challenges and diversity of technologies
column7: Provides “future recommendations” for improving assistive navigation;
column10: Review of Navigation Assistive Tools and Technologies for the Visually Impaired.pdf

column2: Smart Assistive Navigation System for Visually Impaired People
column3: Okolo G.I., Althobaiti T., Ramzan N.
column4: Develop a smart navigation system combining YOLOv8 object detection and audio/tactile guidance to improve safe mobility
column5: Raspberry Pi + camera, ultrasonic & moisture sensors; YOLOv8 object detection; mobile app providing voice-only guidance; tested on nine obstacle types
column6: Achieved 91.7% average accuracy for nine obstacles; provides object type, distance, orientation, surface wetness; supports indoor/outdoor movement
column7: Implies future improvements and broader evaluations, but explicit recommendations not detailed in abstract

column2: Enhancing Accessibility Through Machine Learning: A Review on Visual and Hearing Impairment Technologies
column3: Pal Patel; Shreyansh Pampaniya; Ananya Ghosh; Ritu Raj; Deepa Karuppaih; Saravanakumar Kandasamy
column4: Review ML algorithms for hearing and visual impairment, including YOLO/SSD/RetinaNet and generative AI
column5: Review of SVM, RF, MLP for hearing aids; state-of-the-art object detectors (YOLO, SSD, RetinaNet) and generative AI for accessibility
column6: Highlights transformative potential of deep learning and customized models for personalized assistive solutions
column7: Advocates development/integration of ML-powered assistive tech to enhance QoL and inclusivity
column10: Enhancing Accessibility Through Machine Learning: A Review on Visual and Hearing Impairment Technologies.pdf

column2: Object Detection for the Visually Impaired
column3: Brightson C.
column4: Propose a Flutter-based mobile app using object detection to provide real-time environmental information via TTS and haptics
column5: Mobile app built in Flutter; pre-trained ML model (TFLite suggested) on smartphone camera; TTS for descriptions; haptic feedback; accessible UI
column6: Expected to improve spatial awareness, sense of security, and independence for visually impaired users
column7: Recommends accessible UI, integration with screen readers, and haptic cues
column9: Malawi/India (DMI-St. John the Baptist University is in Malawi)

column2: YOLOInsight: AI-Powered Assistive Device for Visually Impaired Using IoT and Real-Time Object Detection
column3: Gajanan Arsalwad • Saurabh Dabhade • Kabir Shaikh • Sean D'silva
column4: Develop low-cost Raspberry Pi–based real-time object detection and multilingual audio assistant for visually impaired users
column5: Raspberry Pi 4 + camera; YOLO-based detector; OCR; Google TTS; custom NLP assistant; evaluated accuracy and latency
column6: 96% object detection accuracy; 91–95% intent recognition; ~650 ms average response; low-cost and privacy-preserving
column7: Suggests further extension of features, but specific recommendations not fully detailed in abstract
column10: YOLOInsight: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Assistive Device for Visually Impaired Using Internet of Things and Real-Time Object Detection.pdf

column2: Assistive Systems for Visually Impaired Persons: Challenges and Opportunities for Navigation Assistance
column3: Gabriel Iluebe Okolo, Turke Althobaiti, N. Ramzan
column4: Review state‑of‑the‑art assistive technologies and multi‑modal mobility solutions, and discuss challenges/opportunities for navigation
column5: Review of assistive tools, multi‑modal systems, and approaches for indoor/outdoor navigation
column6: Highlights rapid growth of assistive systems and remaining challenges in daily mobility and safety
column7: Provides recommendations for future research
column10: Assistive Systems for Visually Impaired Persons: Challenges and Opportunities for Navigation Assistance.pdf

column2: Review on YOLO‑Based Mobility Assistance Systems for the Visually Impaired
column3: Abhitha Bhat B, Gaurav S B, Shashank Ravindra, Ananya Raghuveer, Nandita Bangera
column4: Review YOLO‑based object detection models for real‑time mobility and spatial awareness with audio feedback for visually impaired users
column5: Literature review of systems using YOLO variants, Darknet + TensorFlow, Google Text‑to‑Speech (gTTS), Raspberry Pi for audio‑feedback‑based navigation
column6: Shows YOLO’s suitability for real‑time assistive navigation where visual data are converted into descriptive audio cues
column7: Emphasizes building effective, real‑time YOLO‑based assistive technologies; specific future work not detailed
column10: Review on YOLO-based Mobility Assistance Systems for the Visually Impaired.pdf

column2: Teleguidance-based remote navigation assistance for visually impaired and blind people—usability and user experience
column3: Babar Chaudary, Sami Pohjolainen, Saima Aziz, Leena Arhippainen & Petri Pulli
column4: Overcome limits of guide dogs, white canes, and basic GPS apps by providing real‑time, context‑aware smartphone navigation
column5: Flutter app; uses Google Vision/Places/Maps APIs for object & crowd detection, nearby places, navigation; Gemini Vision for text/image reading; accelerometer for fall detection; multilingual voice assistance with audio and haptic feedback
column6: Described as easy‑to‑use all‑in‑one assistant; quantitative results not reported in abstract
column7: Future work: offline functionality, more languages, context‑aware navigation (traffic lights, crosswalks, indoor), AI‑based route suggestions and smart‑city integration
column10: Teleguidance-based remote navigation assistance for visually impaired and blind people—usability and user experience.pdf

column2: A shape-changing haptic navigation interface for vision impairment
column3: Spiers, A. J., Quinn, R., Murtough, S., et al.
column4: To evaluate a handheld shape-changing haptic interface that provides directional cues without audio.
column5: Experimental study (n=12); compared shape-changing haptics vs. audio/vibration for navigation tasks.
column6: Achieved parity with sighted vision in navigation accuracy; reduced cognitive load compared to audio-only.
column7: Integrate haptic cues into mobile navigation apps for noisy or privacy-sensitive environments.

column2: YOLO-OD: Obstacle Detection for Visually Impaired Navigation Assistance
column3: Wang, W., Jing, B., Yu, X., et al.
column4: To implement a real-time, high-accuracy obstacle detection system focused on navigation hazards.
column5: Optimization of YOLOv8 for mobile inference; tested on indoor/outdoor obstacle datasets.
column6: Achieved mAP50=0.88; provided fast real-time performance suitable for walking pace navigation.
column7: Combine object detection with depth-sensing models to provide spatial awareness beyond labels.

column2: Real-Time Assistive Navigation for the Visually Impaired: A Scalable Approach for Indoor and Outdoor Mobility
column3: Das, D., Das, A. D., Sadaf, F., Uddin, A., & Mondal, T.
column4: To develop a scalable navigation system that operates entirely offline and provides depth information.
column5: On-device TFLite inference; integrated monocular depth estimation; campus environment testing.
column6: Reduced latency via local processing; achieved low Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for distance estimation.
column7: Use zone-based alerts (Danger/Caution/Safe) to account for sensor noise in mobile cameras.

column2: NaviSense: A Multimodal Assistive Mobile Application for Object Retrieval by Persons with Visual Impairment
column3: Narayanan, A., Qiao, F., et al.
column4: To build a multimodal mobile application that assists visually impaired users in retrieving specific objects and understanding complex scenes.
column5: Implementation of high-accuracy object detection on a mobile-ready pipeline; integration of tactile (vibration) and audio feedback for directional guidance.
column6: Demonstrated that multimodal feedback (combining sound and touch) significantly reduces the time taken to find/retrieve objects compared to audio-only.
column7: Recommends optimizing the processing load on mobile devices and incorporating personalized user detection preferences.

column2: A wearable obstacle avoidance device for visually impaired individuals with cross-modal learning
column3: Gao, Y., Wu, D., Song, J., Hou, B., et al.
column4: To create a wearable system that exceeds the safety of the traditional white cane using cross-modal AI learning.
column5: Developed a wearable system with high-speed sensors and Cross-modal Learning; tested against "sudden obstacles" vs. white cane.
column6: Achieved a 100% collision avoidance rate (vs. 26% for white cane) for sudden obstacles; system latency <320ms.
column7: Recommended for high-speed navigation and for use in busy environments where traditional canes are too slow.

column2: PathFinder: Designing a map-less navigation system for blind people in unfamiliar buildings
column3: Kuribayashi, M., Ishihara, T., Sato, D., et al.
column4: To design a navigation system that works without pre-existing maps, helping users in unfamiliar indoor environments.
column5: Map-less navigation algorithm; utilized on-device sensors to detect landmarks; tested with blind participants in multi-story office buildings.
column6: Successfully navigated unfamiliar routes with minimal assistance; proved real-time environment understanding is flexible.
column7: Recommended for improving building accessibility through automated landmark descriptions.

column2: NaviGPT: A Real-time AI-driven Mobile Navigation System for Persons with Visual Impairment
column3: Zhang, H., Falletta, N. J., Xie, J., et al.
column4: To explore the effectiveness of Large Vision-Language Models (GPT-4) in providing high-level scene reasoning.
column5: Mobile app sending frames to cloud server (GPT-4 API); path-planning tests with 16 blind participants.
column6: High satisfaction for scene descriptions, but participants complained about high latency (2-5s) and cloud dependency.
column7: Recommends moving toward fully offline, on-device models (like YOLO) to ensure reliability and low latency.

column2: PC-CS-YOLO: High-Precision Obstacle Detection for Visually Impaired Safety
column3: Li, J., Zheng, M., Dong, D., & Xie, X.
column4: To improve the detection accuracy for thin or small hazards (like poles) that standard object detection models often miss.
column5: Specialized PC-CS-YOLO architecture; enhanced small-object features; tested on custom urban navigation hazard dataset.
column6: Achieved higher precision for small hazards while staying under 25ms per frame.
column7: Assistive devices should prioritize "thin hazard" detection to prevent signpost or railing collisions.

column2: An RGB-D Camera-Based Wearable Device for Visually Impaired People: Enhanced Navigation with Reduced Social Stigma
column3: Li, Z., Han, F., & Zheng, K.
column4: To develop a wearable device that improves independent travel and reduces the social stigma associated with traditional white canes.
column5: Integrated RGB-D camera and IMU with YOLO-based recognition; Intelligent interaction module to identify the "core obstacle."
column6: Achieved significantly lower collision rates for mid-air obstacles compared to white canes and ultrasonic sensors.
column7: Replaces the traditional cane with an arm-mounted design to reduce disability labeling and enhance spatial perception.

column2: SnapStick: Merging AI and Accessibility to Enhance Navigation for Blind Users
column3: Shafique, S., Bailo, G. L., Zanchi, S., et al.
column4: To evaluate a smart cane integrated with Vision-Language Models (VLM) for enhanced spatial perception.
column5: Used Florence-2 VLM for scene description; tested with 11 blind participants; utilized bone-conduction headphones.
column6: Achieved 94% accuracy in environmental awareness; received high SUS score (84.7%) for usability.
column7: Recommends VLM integration for "complex reasoning" tasks like reading bus routes or avoiding specific hazards.

column2: A Survey on Deep Learning-based Smart Assistive Aids for Visually Impaired Individuals
column3: Aetesam Ali Khan Ashar, Asir Abrar, Jiangjiang Liu
column4: Survey deep learning-based smart assistive aids (smart canes, wearables) for visually impaired individuals, focusing on object detection and navigation strategies.
column5: Literature survey of AI-based assistive devices using ML algorithms (YOLO, SSD) for object detection via cameras; reviewed use of ultrasonic, IR laser, and rain sensors for obstacle detection.
column6: Smart canes with deep learning-based object detection show promising results for safe navigation; YOLO and SSD models effectively identify obstacles; continued research could enable full independent travel.
column7: Calls for continued research to enhance visually impaired persons' ability to interact with surroundings and travel independently through improved sensor and AI integration.

column2: A Wearable Visually Impaired Assistive System Based on Semantic Vision SLAM for Grasping Operation
column3: Fei Fei, Sifan Xian, Ruonan Yang, Changcheng Wu, Xiong Lu
column4: Develop a wearable assistive system to help visually impaired individuals perceive and grasp target objects within a tabletop environment.
column5: Semantic visual SLAM algorithm fusing ORB-SLAM2 and YOLOv5s for semantic map construction; depth camera integrated into wearable; vibration array feedback for directional guidance; Dobot Magician manipulator for grasping tasks.
column6: System demonstrated feasibility in localization, semantic mapping, and grasping tasks; vibration feedback effectively conveyed directional information; experiments verified effectiveness in simulated visually impaired grasping scenarios.
column7: Suggests broader real-world testing and integration of more complex environments; recommends extending system to support a wider range of objects and dynamic settings.

column2: A Comprehensive Review of Navigation Systems for Visually Impaired Individuals
column3: Mustufa Haider Abidi, Arshad Noor Siddiquee, Hisham Alkhalefah, Vishwaraj Srivastava
column4: Categorize and assess navigation assistance solutions for visually impaired individuals, emphasizing electronic systems employing sensors, AI, and feedback mechanisms.
column5: Navigation solutions segmented into four categories: Visual Imagery Systems, Non-Visual Data Systems, Map-Based Solutions, and 3D Sound Systems; reviewed integration of ultrasonic sensors, LiDAR, and smartphone-based navigation satellite systems.
column6: Significant evolution in navigation aids; modern electronic systems highly effective for obstacle detection and safe navigation; smartphone-based solutions are portable and convenient; navigation satellite systems enhance navigation assistance.
column7: Advocates for continued innovation and technological integration in navigation tools; emphasizes need for futuristic solutions to empower visually impaired individuals with increased independence.

column2: An Artificial Intelligence-based Assistant for the Visually Impaired
column3: Luis Marquez-Carpintero, Francisco Gomez-Donoso, Zuria Bauer, Bessie Dominguez-Dager, Alvaro Belmonte-Baeza, Mónica Pina-Navarro, Francisco Morillas-Espejo, Felix Escalona, Miguel Cazorla
column4: Develop AIDEN, an AI-based mobile assistant application aimed at improving quality of life for visually impaired individuals by enabling object identification, text reading, and environmental navigation.
column5: YOLO architectures for object detection; Large Language and Vision Assistant (LLAVA) for scene understanding; multimodal interaction methods for text and visual information access; user feedback evaluation.
column6: AIDEN enhances user autonomy and access to information; positive user feedback confirms improved daily usability; system effectively identifies objects, reads text, and answers environmental questions.
column7: Recommends broader user trials and further integration of contextual reasoning; suggests expanding language support and improving real-time response for complex environments.

column2: Independent Pathfinding with Collision Avoidance for Visually Impaired Individuals
column3: Tadeh Ghahremanians, Hossein Mahvash Mohammadi
column4: Propose a panoptic segmentation framework as foundation for an effective pathfinding system that combines robust collision avoidance for visually impaired individuals.
column5: Single-stage instance segmentation using ResNet101-FPN encoder-decoder architecture; customized panoptic labeled dataset; evaluation using Panoptic Quality (PQ) metric under varied weather conditions.
column6: Method surpasses recent panoptic segmentation techniques by 4.092 PQ points; outperforms existing pathfinding systems in accuracy and efficiency; demonstrates robustness under varied weather conditions.
column7: Recommends future integration with real-time feedback in visual prostheses; suggests expanding dataset and testing in more complex real-world environments.

column2: Leveraging Assistive Technology for Visually Impaired People through Optimal Deep Transfer Learning Based Object Detection Model
column3: Mahir Mohammed Sharif Adam, Nojood O. Aljehane, Mohammed Yahya Alzahrani, Samah Al Zanin
column4: Develop EATBP-ODHOA, an effective object detection model for visually impaired individuals using advanced deep learning and a Hiking Optimization Algorithm for parameter tuning.
column5: Adaptive Bilateral Filtering (ABF) for image preprocessing; Faster R-CNN for object detection; fusion of ResNet and DenseNet-201 for feature extraction; Bi-GRU for classification; Hiking Optimisation Algorithm (HOA) for parameter tuning; tested on indoor object detection dataset.
column6: EATBP-ODHOA achieved superior accuracy of 99.25% compared to existing approaches on the indoor object detection dataset.
column7: Recommends deployment in real-world assistive devices; suggests extending the model to outdoor environments and testing on larger, more diverse datasets.

column2: Obstacle Detection System for Navigation Assistance of Visually Impaired People Based on Deep Learning Techniques
column3: Yahia Said, Mohamed Atri, Marwan Ali Albahar, Ahmed Ben Atitallah, Yazan Ahmad Alsariera
column4: Propose an intelligent navigation assistance system for visually impaired people using deep learning and Neural Architecture Search (NAS) for optimal object detection architecture.
column5: Fast NAS based on reinforcement learning to search optimal anchor-free object detection architecture; feature pyramid network optimization; evaluated on COCO and Indoor Object Detection and Recognition (IODR) dataset.
column6: Searched model outperformed original by 2.6% in average precision (AP) while maintaining acceptable computational efficiency; system provides reliable real-time navigation assistance.
column7: Suggests integrating the system into portable wearable devices; recommends further optimization for edge deployment to reduce latency in real-world navigation scenarios.

column2: Real-Time Assistive Navigation for the Visually Impaired: A Scalable Approach for Indoor and Outdoor Mobility
column3: Dabbrata Das, Argho Deb Das, Farhan Sadaf, Azhar Uddin, Tirtho Mondal
column4: Develop PathFinder, a fully offline, mapless mobile navigation system for blind and low-vision individuals that operates without internet dependency.
column5: On-device TFLite inference; monocular depth estimation for obstacle-free path identification; pathfinding algorithm for route selection; usability study with 15 BLV participants in indoor and outdoor environments.
column6: Reduced MAE for distance estimation; 73% of participants learned to operate in under a minute; 80% praised accuracy and responsiveness; demonstrated real-time performance indoors and outdoors.
column7: Recommends zone-based alerts (Danger/Caution/Safe) to handle sensor noise; suggests improving performance in complex indoor layouts and low-light conditions.

column2: Turn-by-Turn Indoor Navigation for the Visually Impaired
column3: Santosh Srinivasaiah, Sai Kumar Nekkanti, Rohith Reddy Nedhunuri
column4: Introduce a novel turn-by-turn indoor navigation system for visually impaired individuals using only a smartphone camera without relying on GPS.
column5: Smartphone camera captures real-time images sent to Raspberry Pi; on-device LLM, multimodal models, and deep learning for architectural feature/signage/obstacle detection; LLM generates natural language instructions delivered via audio prompts.
column6: Preliminary evaluations demonstrate effectiveness in accurately guiding users through complex indoor spaces; minimal workload on user device; compatible with all device types including those incapable of running AI models.
column7: Recommends scaling to more complex indoor environments and improving landmark recognition; suggests integrating offline model updates to maintain data privacy.

column2: Vision-Based Smart Wearable Assistive Navigation System Using Deep Learning for Visually Impaired People
column3: Syed Salman Shah, Abid Imran, Saad-Ur-Rehman, Arsalan Arif, Khurram Khan, Muhammad Arsalan, Sajjad Manzoor, Ghulam Jawad Sirewal
column4: Propose a smart wearable assistive navigation system integrating object detection, depth sensing, and audio feedback to enhance mobility and independence for visually impaired individuals.
column5: YOLOv5n with hyperparameter fine-tuning and transfer learning on Jetson Nano; depth camera for distance measurement; voice module for auditory alerts; Tensor-RT optimization for real-time deployment.
column6: mAP@50 improved from 0.457 to 0.845 and mAP@50-95 from 0.28 to 0.593 after fine-tuning; Tensor-RT optimization increased frame rate for real-time use; system successfully alerts users to hazards and obstacles.
column7: Recommends addressing Jetson Nano compatibility issues with newer YOLO models; suggests expanding the object class database and testing in diverse real-world environments.
